articles.title: Australia Raises Rates to 4.85%, Highest Since 2008
articles.excerpt: The Reserve Bank of Australia split 6-3 on its fifth hike of 2026 and now sees inflation above its target range until late 2027.
articles.body_md:
The Reserve Bank of Australia raised its cash rate by 25 basis points to 4.85% on Tuesday, the bank's [policy statement](https://www.rba.gov.au/media-releases/2026/mr-26-30.html) shows. That is the highest level since November 2008, [CNBC reported](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/03/australia-hikes-rates-18-year-high-finflation.html).

The vote was not close to unanimous. Six board members backed the hike and three wanted to hold at 4.60%, the statement says. [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/03/australia-hikes-rates-18-year-high-finflation.html) counted it as the fifth increase this year.

**How the cash rate works**

The cash rate is what banks charge each other for overnight loans. When the RBA lifts it, mortgage and business loan rates in Australia tend to follow. That squeezes spending, which is the point: less demand is meant to cool prices.

**Why the board moved now**

Prices are still running hot. Consumer prices rose 4.3% in the year to September, up from 4% in August, [CNBC reported](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/03/australia-hikes-rates-18-year-high-finflation.html). The bank now expects inflation to stay above 3% for the coming year and does not see it reaching the top of its 2% to 3% target range until late 2027, about three quarters later than it forecast before.

The statement names three drivers. Fuel and commodity prices are higher because of the Middle East conflict. Firms report cost pressure and plan to pass it on. AI-related investment is pushing up prices for technology goods.

*In our opinion: A 6-3 split says the board is no longer sure how much more Australia can take. The stake is wider than one country, because the RBA blamed oil and AI spending, two forces hitting every central bank at once. The next signal to watch is Australia's monthly inflation print, which will show whether the board has to move again.*

The cost lands on households. The statement says housing prices have fallen significantly and unemployment has risen, and it expects growth to slow further. Asked about a recession, Governor Michelle Bullock said it is "not our base case at the moment," [CNBC reported](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/03/australia-hikes-rates-18-year-high-finflation.html).

articles.title: SEC Staff Say Token Voters Usually Aren't a 'Central Party'
articles.excerpt: Three new staff answers, added Nov. 2, list the powers that make someone a central party. The SEC notes the FAQs carry no legal force.
articles.body_md:
People who vote with governance tokens generally do not count as a "central party" under SEC guidance, Corporation Finance staff said in three [answers added Nov. 2](https://www.sec.gov/about/divisions-offices/division-corporation-finance/faqs-crypto-assets) to their crypto FAQ.

That label matters. The SEC's March 17 interpretive release says a digital commodity is not itself a security and runs on a "functional" crypto system with no central party overseeing it. Find a central party, and that argument gets harder.

**How the test works**

The release defines a central party as a person or group with operational, economic or voting control of a system. The new answers say token voters generally aren't such a group if they are unaffiliated and have no deal, formal or informal, to act together. Delegating votes to one another counts as acting together. The same holds when voting runs through a foundation and is based on holding the native token.

Even a group needs real control to qualify, the staff wrote.

The answers also list what "overseeing participation" looks like. A central party has unilateral power to grant or limit access, change voting rules for upgrades or token distributions, pick who validates transactions, or rewrite code, reverse transactions and revoke access. Code that runs automatically, or choices made only through broad token voting, generally don't count.

A third answer separates "functional" from "decentralized." Functional means the token works on the system as designed. Decentralized means no one has control. A functional system has some traits of decentralization, but the degree can vary, the staff wrote.

There is a limit. The FAQ says it reflects staff views, is not an SEC rule, and has "no legal force or effect." [CoinMarketCap](https://coinmarketcap.com/academy/article/sec-staff-token-governance-not-central-party) also reported the update.

*In our opinion: The SEC staff just wrote the bouncer's checklist, and an admin key with the power to reverse transactions is the fastest way to get turned away. The stake is every governance token that leans on the digital commodity label. Watch whether the Commission itself puts this test into a rule, because staff answers can be rewritten as easily as they were added.*

articles.title: Crypto.com to Close Its Hong Kong Consumer App on Feb. 1
articles.excerpt: Retail users get about three months to withdraw. Crypto.com's Hong Kong unit is still seeking an SFC license for its institutional exchange.
articles.body_md:
Crypto.com will stop offering its consumer app to users in Hong Kong on Feb. 1, 2027, the company said Monday, [Bloomberg reported](https://news.bloomberglaw.com/crypto/crypto-com-to-shutter-consumer-app-in-hong-kong-in-february). That leaves retail customers about three months to close accounts.

The company framed it as a business call. "This decision reflects our ongoing efforts to optimize global operations and allocate resources where we see the most sustainable long-term opportunities," a spokesperson said, according to Bloomberg. Customers have been notified and will get instructions for closing accounts and withdrawing funds, the spokesperson said.

**Not a full exit**

Crypto.com is keeping a foot in the city. Its unit Foris DAX HK Limited is still seeking a virtual asset trading platform license from the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC), Hong Kong's markets regulator, for its institutional Crypto.com Exchange, [The Straits Times](https://www.straitstimes.com/business/crypto-com-to-shutter-consumer-app-in-hong-kong-in-february) reported, carrying the Bloomberg story. The app closure does not affect that application, [Investing.com](https://uk.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/cryptocom-to-exit-hong-kong-consumer-app-citing-operations--bloomberg-93CH-4950187) reported.

**How Hong Kong's licensing works**

Hong Kong requires any platform that trades crypto for customers in the city to hold an SFC license. Licensed venues face rules on custody, which tokens retail users can buy, and how client money is kept apart from company money. Serving everyday traders under those rules costs more than serving a smaller set of professional clients.

The reports did not include comment from the SFC.

*In our opinion: A global exchange giving up a city's retail users while still chasing that city's license tells you where the money is. Hong Kong has courted crypto firms for years, so the stake is whether its rules leave room for retail apps at scale. Watch the SFC's public license register for a decision on Foris DAX HK.*

For users, the practical step is simple. Move funds before the Feb. 1 cutoff, following the company's instructions.

articles.title: North Korea Denies FBI Finding It Stole $6 Billion From Binance
articles.excerpt: Kim Yo Jong called the U.S. claim "absurd rhetoric" and pointed to last year's Bybit case. The FBI has published 628 addresses tied to the theft.
articles.body_md:
North Korea on Monday rejected the FBI's finding that its hackers stole more than $6 billion in crypto from Binance, calling it "a grave political provocation." The statement came from Kim Yo Jong, a senior Workers' Party official and the sister of leader Kim Jong Un.

State news agency [KCNA](http://www.kcna.kp/en/article/detail/873496f71f6ab3e667a4271b5a4cf4c6) carried it early Tuesday, Pyongyang time. South Korea's [Yonhap](https://en.yna.co.kr/view/AEN20261103000600315) reported the same remarks. They answer the [FBI alert of Oct. 31](https://www.fbi.gov/investigate/cyber/alerts/2026/north-korea-responsible-for-6-billion-binance-attack), which said North Korea was behind the Oct. 29 theft. Black Mint [reported that alert](https://blackmint.markets/news/fbi-north-korea-binance-hack/) the same day.

**Kim pointed to Bybit and the U.S. bitcoin reserve**

Kim said the U.S. claim was "absurd rhetoric and nothing new." She cited last year's Bybit theft, which the FBI [also tied to North Korea](https://www.ic3.gov/PSA/2025/PSA250226), as another case of Washington blaming Pyongyang. She said her government opposes "malicious acts in cyberspace."

She also told readers to look at who would end up holding the coins if they are recovered, citing the U.S. plan to keep seized crypto in a strategic reserve. The statement named no one and gave no details to back that point. It closed by saying North Korea has "issues to reconsider" in its stance toward the U.S.

**How investigators name a hacker**

Blockchains are public. Every transfer of the stolen coins can be followed from address to address. Tracing firms and the FBI compare the route, the tools and the timing with earlier thefts tied to known groups. The FBI calls this one TraderTraitor, the same name it gave the team behind the $1.5 billion Bybit theft in February 2025.

The bureau, working with the Secret Service and IRS Criminal Investigation, published 628 addresses linked to the Binance funds. It asked exchanges, node operators and DeFi services to block any transaction tied to them. A denial from Pyongyang doesn't change that list.

No new statement from the FBI on Kim's remarks appeared on its [cyber alerts page](https://www.fbi.gov/investigate/cyber/alerts) when Black Mint checked Monday evening. The Oct. 31 alert was still posted there.

*In our opinion: the U.S. case rests on public on-chain tracing, and Kim's statement offers no data of its own to test against it. The stake now is practical: the more services that honor the 628-address block list, the harder it gets to cash out $6 billion. Watch the FBI's list for updates, since any change would show where the coins moved after Monday.*

articles.title: New Jersey Drops Coinbase Staking Order and $5 Million Penalty
articles.excerpt: The Oct. 30 notice is "without prejudice," so the state can sue again. California, Maryland, Wisconsin and Washington still have staking cases open.
articles.body_md:
New Jersey's securities regulator rescinded its 2023 order against Coinbase's staking service on Oct. 30, dropping a $5 million penalty, a [signed notice](https://assets.ctfassets.net/sygt3q11s4a9/UP8DDH65wMBLgeI2RbWRR/90945f6360884dfa75aadcbac57d4f9f/Coinbase_Withdrawal_Order_10_30_26.pdf) shows. The order had kept New Jersey customers from staking new funds since 2023.

The notice is "without prejudice." It makes no ruling on the merits, and Acting Bureau Chief Keith A. Alt keeps the power to bring a new case.

**How staking works, and why a state objected**

Proof-of-stake networks such as Ethereum and Solana pay rewards to holders who lock up coins to help confirm transactions. Coinbase does the locking for customers and keeps a cut of the rewards as its fee. In June 2023, New Jersey's Bureau of Securities said that service was a security that had to be registered before it could be sold in the state.

The money is real. Coinbase booked $85.7 million in blockchain rewards revenue in the third quarter, down 54% from $184.6 million a year earlier, its [quarterly filing](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1679788/000167978826000122/coin-20260930.htm) shows. The company blamed lower prices and reward rates, mainly for Solana and ether.

**Four states are still on the list**

Ten states moved against Coinbase staking in June 2023, the filing says. Alabama, Illinois, Kentucky, South Carolina and Vermont dropped their actions in March and April 2025. California, Maryland and Wisconsin still have agreements that bar new staking, and Washington's case is open, according to the filing and [BeInCrypto](https://beincrypto.com/new-jersey-drops-coinbase-staking-lawsuit/).

Coinbase's filing says New Jersey told the company on Oct. 29 that it planned to rescind. It also says Coinbase disputes the state regulators' claims and will "vigorously defend" against them.

Neither the notice nor the filing sets a date for New Jersey customers to start staking new funds.

*In our opinion: New Jersey got its staking back on paper before it got a date. The bigger stake sits in the four states still holding out, since each one keeps a slice of Coinbase customers out of a product that brought in $85.7 million last quarter. Watch Coinbase's state eligibility list: New Jersey coming off it is the step that turns this order into rewards.*

articles.title: Mercado Bitcoin Freezes Withdrawals as Watchers Flag a $40M Drain
articles.excerpt: Brazil's Mercado Bitcoin paused deposits and withdrawals after a security incident. It says clients lost nothing. Hypernative counts more than $40M moved.
articles.body_md:
Brazilian crypto exchange Mercado Bitcoin suspended deposits and withdrawals on Monday after what it called a security incident in one of its systems, as outside trackers flagged more than $40 million in outflows.

In an [official statement on X](https://x.com/MercadoBitcoin/status/2117239507263132056) posted at 7:56 a.m. ET, the exchange said in Portuguese that it found and contained the incident overnight, that clients suffered no losses and that no data leaked. It has not given a loss figure. It has not called the event a hack.

Outside trackers put numbers on it. Blockchain security firm Hypernative estimated that more than $40 million left wallets it ties to the exchange, according to an alert [shared by Opsek founder Pablo Sabbatella](https://x.com/PabloSabbatella/status/2117241590787846164) and [reported by Unchained](https://unchainedcrypto.com/mercado-bitcoin-halts-withdrawals-over-security-incident-as-hypernative-flags-40-million-drain/). Arkham Intelligence groups 36 addresses holding about $46 million, [The Defiant reported](https://thedefiant.io/news/hacks/arkham-says-mercado-bitcoin-attacker-holds-46-million). Mercado Bitcoin has not confirmed either figure.

Hypernative's count includes about 2,852 ETH, 106 BTC, 10,700 SOL and 6.7 million XLM, plus more than 200 other tokens, spread across at least 10 chains. The 106 BTC alone is worth roughly $8.2 million at Monday's price near $77,400, based on CoinGecko data.

How did the money move? Hypernative described the outflows as plain transfers rather than a smart contract exploit. In plain words, whoever moved the funds appears to have had the power to sign transactions from the exchange's own wallets, the way the exchange itself would. A smart contract exploit, by contrast, tricks a program's code into paying out. Hypernative said it was still unclear how that signing access was obtained. Most of the funds moved in a 34-minute window starting at 1:19 a.m. ET, it said.

About 90 minutes after its first post, the exchange [published the destination addresses](https://x.com/MercadoBitcoin/status/2117261565200146525) on EVM networks, Bitcoin, Solana, Stellar and Tron so others can track them. It says it is working with authorities and will reopen once it is safe.

The pause lands four days after Binance's Oct. 29 hot-wallet drain. No one has tied the two events together.

*In our opinion:* The exchange's promise that clients lost nothing is the line to hold it to, and the fastest proof is a dated reopening with balances intact. Publishing the addresses early was the right call, since it gives trackers and other exchanges a head start on freezing funds. Watch for a loss figure and an explanation of how signing keys were reached, because that answer matters to every exchange running hot wallets.

articles.title: Strategy Is Back With 811 BTC, but $208M Went to Its Own Stock
articles.excerpt: After a week off, Strategy bought 811 BTC for $65.5M at an average $80,846. It also spent $208.2M buying back STRC preferred shares.
articles.body_md:
Strategy's week off is over. The largest corporate bitcoin holder bought 811 BTC for $65.5 million between Oct. 26 and Nov. 1, at an average of $80,846 per coin, according to a [Form 8-K filed Monday with the SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1050446/000119312526442707/mstr-20261102.htm).

That brings its stack to 849,327 BTC, bought for $64.08 billion at an average of $75,451. With bitcoin near $77,400 on Monday, per CoinGecko, the holding is worth about $65.8 billion, roughly $1.7 billion above cost. This week's coins were bought above Monday's price, so that batch starts slightly underwater. Timing the market is hard, even for a company built around it.

Follow the cash and the picture gets more interesting. Strategy sold 1,178,552 common shares through its at-the-market program, which lets a company sell new stock into the market a little at a time. That raised $164.0 million. Only $65.5 million went to bitcoin. The other $98.5 million went to a cash pile the company keeps for general use.

It then spent $208.2 million of that cash buying back 2,092,035 shares of STRC (its variable-rate preferred stock). Preferred stock pays a set dividend and ranks ahead of common shares. Buying it back shrinks the dividend bill the company owes each month. The filing says $748.6 million of preferred buyback room remains.

Separately, Strategy keeps a dollar reserve to cover preferred dividends and debt interest. It used $43.4 million of that reserve for dividends during the week, leaving $4.79 billion. General-purpose cash ended the week at $132.7 million.

So the headline buy was the smaller number. More money went into retiring preferred stock than into bitcoin.

*In our opinion:* Strategy is running two jobs now, bitcoin buyer and manager of its own dividend obligations, and this week the second job got the bigger budget. That is not a retreat from bitcoin, but it shows the company weighing what its preferred stock costs against what another coin is worth. Watch next Monday's filing for whether the buyback keeps outpacing the bitcoin buys.
articles.author: Blackmint Desk

articles.title: Standard Chartered Lets Hong Kong Firms Move Bank Deposits 24/7
articles.excerpt: The bank's new tokenised deposits settle between banks around the clock in central bank money, as the HKMA widens its Ensemble TX pilot to 12 banks.
articles.body_md:
Banks close at night. Standard Chartered's corporate clients in Hong Kong can now move money 24 hours a day anyway.

The bank [launched tokenised deposits](https://www.sc.com/en/press-release/standard-chartered-launches-tokenised-deposits-in-hong-kong/) on Monday, making Hong Kong the first market in the group to offer the service to companies. It said it plans to expand to more markets over time.

The launch came the same day the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA), the city's central bank, [said its Ensemble TX pilot](https://www.hkma.gov.hk/eng/news-and-media/press-releases/2026/11/20261102-5/) can now settle tokenised deposit trades between banks 24 hours a day in tokenised central bank money. The pilot now counts 12 participating banks and 20 other firms, the HKMA said. Five banks joined this year, [according to its list](https://www.hkma.gov.hk/media/eng/doc/key-functions/ifc/fintech/cbdc/EnsembleTX_AnnexA_eng.pdf).

How does it work? A tokenised deposit is ordinary money in a regulated bank account, recorded as a digital token on a blockchain. When a client sends it to a customer of another bank, the token moves at once. Behind the scenes, the two banks settle what they owe each other in central bank money, the safest form of money in the system. Until now, that bank-to-bank step mostly waited for business hours. That is different from a stablecoin, which is a token issued by a private company and backed by reserves it holds.

Standard Chartered said China AMC, Finloop and PantherTrade have already run live tokenised deposit transactions, including settling tokenised money market funds. Fireblocks, a digital asset custody firm, is connecting the service to crypto clients, and Hashkey has joined, the bank said. It did not disclose transaction values, [Global Custodian](https://www.globalcustodian.com/standard-chartered-launches-tokenised-deposits-in-hong-kong/) and other outlets noted.

The move follows HSBC's Hong Kong dollar stablecoin push last month, giving the city two big banks testing different ways to put money on-chain.

*In our opinion:* Banks are making their case that companies don't need a stablecoin to get money that moves at midnight, because the bank deposit itself can do it. The missing piece is size, since no transaction values were shared. Watch whether the HKMA or the bank publishes volumes, which would show if treasurers actually use the night shift.

articles.title: Nvidia and Costco Join 50 Issuers Blocking OKXICE Stock Tokens
articles.excerpt: The venue's Oct. 30 notice still names no start date for trading, and it says its access-token contract has not been checked by outside auditors.
articles.body_md:
Fifty public companies have now told the tokenized stock venue run by Intercontinental Exchange and OKX not to trade their shares, according to a [public notice dated Oct. 30](https://www.okx.com/cdn/assets/okfe/web3-activities/okxicetsv/notices/OKXICE_Tokenized_Securities_Venue_Public_Notice_26.10.30.pdf).

The list stood at 38 in the venue's Oct. 28 notice, [Unchained reported](https://unchainedcrypto.com/nvidia-costco-and-10-more-issuers-opt-out-of-ice-and-okxs-tokenized-stock-venue/) on Monday. The 12 new names include Nvidia, Costco, Nike, Micron, CrowdStrike, Palo Alto Networks and Reddit. They sit beside earlier objectors such as Microsoft, Alphabet, JPMorgan Chase, Goldman Sachs and Walmart. The notice gives no reason for any objection, and it still lists no date for trading to begin.

**How the opt-out works**

The venue, OKXICE TSV, plans to let identity-checked wallets trade stock tokens against stablecoins in pools on OKX's XLayer network. The tokens are made by outside firms, not by the venue. Under the SEC exemptive order the venue relies on, a company that files a timely objection keeps its stock off the venue whenever an unaffiliated third party did the tokenizing, [according to Unchained](https://unchainedcrypto.com/nvidia-costco-and-10-more-issuers-opt-out-of-ice-and-okxs-tokenized-stock-venue/).

**Who gets paid**

Traders pay the venue a flat-rate service fee on each trade, plus a pool fee that goes to liquidity providers and a network fee for the blockchain, the [notice](https://www.okx.com/cdn/assets/okfe/web3-activities/okxicetsv/notices/OKXICE_Tokenized_Securities_Venue_Public_Notice_26.10.30.pdf) says. It adds that no ICE or OKX affiliate will act as a liquidity provider for now.

**What the notice warns**

The venue says it is "not registered with the Securities and Exchange Commission" for this activity. Its access-token contract "has been audited internally, but not by external auditors." If the broker-dealer behind a token failed, whether tokens held in a self-custody wallet would count as protected customer property "is uncertain."

The venue's own position is that its tokens are "not restricted to trading on OKXICE TSV," so other venues can support them if the tokenizer agrees and the SEC conditions are met.

*In our opinion:* Fifty refusals before a single trade tells you who holds the lever here, and it isn't the exchange. The SEC order gave issuers a veto over third-party tokens, and blue-chip names are using it while the rules are new. Watch the next notice for a launch date, and for the first big company that tokenizes its own shares instead of saying no.

articles.title: HSBC Says RedCoin Stablecoin Hit 50,000 Users in Its First Week
articles.excerpt: The Hong Kong dollar token reached about 1.5% of PayMe's 3.3 million users, and HSBC plans to put it in its main banking app next.
articles.body_md:
HSBC's RedCoin stablecoin signed up 50,000 users in just over a week, Group CEO Georges Elhedery said Monday at Hong Kong FinTech Week, [the South China Morning Post reported](https://www.scmp.com/business/banking-finance/article/3372972/hsbcs-redcoin-stablecoin-draws-50000-users-first-week-bank-deepens-local-tech-push).

The Hong Kong dollar token went live Oct. 23 inside PayMe, the bank's payments app, which has more than 3.3 million users. That puts the early count at about 1.5% of the app's reach. [TokenPost](https://www.tokenpost.com/news/business/46268) reported the same figure and noted that the 3.3 million is potential reach, not RedCoin users.

"Of course, our target is multimillion users," Elhedery said, [according to the SCMP](https://www.scmp.com/business/banking-finance/article/3372972/hsbcs-redcoin-stablecoin-draws-50000-users-first-week-bank-deepens-local-tech-push). He credited the "comfortable" rules set by the Hong Kong Monetary Authority for the quick start.

**How RedCoin works**

Each RedCoin is meant to be redeemable for one Hong Kong dollar and runs on HSBC's private, permissioned blockchain, [TokenPost reported](https://www.tokenpost.com/news/business/46268). A PayMe user turns on a wallet inside the app with no minimum balance, then can send coins to friends or pay at more than 100,000 merchants. Nobody needs a separate crypto wallet.

**What comes next**

HSBC plans to offer RedCoin in its HSBC HK Mobile Banking app and to let customers use it to buy tokenized funds, including a money market fund, [both outlets reported](https://www.scmp.com/business/banking-finance/article/3372972/hsbcs-redcoin-stablecoin-draws-50000-users-first-week-bank-deepens-local-tech-push). Elhedery said it would later reach all HSBC and Hang Seng Bank clients but gave no timetable.

HSBC is one of two licensed stablecoin issuers in the city. The other, Anchorpoint, a venture of Standard Chartered, Animoca Brands and HKT, opened beta access to its HKDAP coin in August and is aiming for retail use "as early as end-2026," [the SCMP reported](https://www.scmp.com/business/banking-finance/article/3372972/hsbcs-redcoin-stablecoin-draws-50000-users-first-week-bank-deepens-local-tech-push).

The bank did not say how many of the 50,000 have actually paid with the coin.

*In our opinion:* Fifty thousand sign-ups is a solid week for a coin that arrived inside an app people already had, though a wallet opened out of curiosity is the digital cousin of a January gym card. The figure that counts is spending, so watch for HSBC to report payment volume and to put a date on the banking-app rollout. If both of Hong Kong's licensed issuers reach retail by year end, the city becomes a live test of bank-issued coins against dollar tokens.

articles.title: Indonesia Inflation Eases to 3.23% as Core Prices Cool Past Forecasts
articles.excerpt: Core inflation fell to 2.56%, a six-month low, while chilies, rice and gasoline kept the headline rate near the top of Bank Indonesia's target band.
articles.body_md:
Indonesia's annual inflation eased to 3.23% in October from 3.28% in September, Statistics Indonesia said Monday, [Tempo reported](https://en.tempo.co/read/2122819/food-prices-drive-indonesias-inflation-to-3-23-in-october).

Economists had expected 3.29%, according to [Trading Economics](https://tradingeconomics.com/indonesia/inflation-cpi/news/597098). Core inflation fell to 2.56% from 2.84%, a six-month low and below the 2.75% forecast. Prices rose 0.22% from September.

**What pushed prices**

Food, drinks and tobacco rose 4.82% from a year earlier and added 1.40 percentage points to the total, led by bird's eye chilies, fresh fish, rice, cooking oil, chicken and beef, [CNBC Indonesia reported](https://www.cnbcindonesia.com/news/20261102112044-4-781465/inflasi-tahunan-ri-323-di-oktober-mepet-target-bi-pemerintah). Transport climbed 4.87%, mostly on gasoline and airfares. Gold jewelry lifted personal care costs 4.52%. Every province saw annual inflation, from 2.52% in Jakarta to 8.07% in North Sulawesi.

**How the target works**

Bank Indonesia and the government aim for 2.5% inflation, give or take one point, so the band runs from 1.5% to 3.5%, [CNBC Indonesia noted](https://www.cnbcindonesia.com/news/20261102112044-4-781465/inflasi-tahunan-ri-323-di-oktober-mepet-target-bi-pemerintah). The headline rate sits near the ceiling. Core inflation strips out volatile food and government-set prices like fuel, so central bankers read it as a gauge of underlying demand. On that measure the news is better: prices are cooling.

Volatile food rose 5.81%, the fastest of the three components, while government-set prices rose 3.24%, [Tempo reported](https://en.tempo.co/read/2122819/food-prices-drive-indonesias-inflation-to-3-23-in-october).

For crypto traders, bitcoin was at $77,937 at 5:54 a.m. ET, little changed over 24 hours, according to [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/bitcoin).

*In our opinion:* The headline number looks tight, but the core reading is the one that moves a central bank, and it fell further than forecasters expected. That gives Bank Indonesia more room than a chili-driven headline would imply, as long as food costs stop climbing. Watch the next rate decision and the rupiah, because a central bank's room to cut also depends on its currency.

articles.title: BTCPay Server Ties Hot Wallet Drains to Versions 2.4.1 and Older
articles.excerpt: Attackers logged in as admin on some self-hosted servers and swept hot wallets. BTCPay says it has no credible drain reports on the newest 2.4.7 release.
articles.body_md:
BTCPay Server told merchants on Sunday that attackers swept hot wallets on instances running version 2.4.1 or older, a release from July 23. No loss total or count of hit servers has been published.

The first alert came at 5:25 p.m. ET on X. "We are receiving reports of hot wallets on BTCPay Servers being swept by unauthorized attackers," the project [posted](https://x.com/BtcpayServer/status/2117020340815819262), and it asked operators to shut their servers down until it finished looking.

**What the team found**

Founder Nicolas Dorier [wrote](https://x.com/NicolasDorier/status/2117051298633900041) at 7:28 p.m. ET that the attacker "managed to log in as admin on those instance," and that the team was still working out how. At 11:07 p.m. ET, BTCPay [said](https://x.com/BtcpayServer/status/2117106238123123008) its investigation found an attack vector aimed at 2.4.1 and older, with "no credible reports of hot wallet drains" on 2.4.7. Some instances run through hosting companies were [shut down automatically](https://x.com/BtcpayServer/status/2117106240098611681).

**How a hot wallet works**

BTCPay is free software that shops run on their own servers to take bitcoin. A hot wallet keeps the key that signs payments on that internet-connected server, so the server can pay out on its own. That is handy. It also means anyone who gets admin control of the server can move the coins.

**Why the version matters**

Version 2.4.2, out Aug. 7, fixed a critical flaw that was already being exploited, according to its [release notes](https://github.com/btcpayserver/btcpayserver/releases/tag/v2.4.2). The August [advisory](https://blog.btcpayserver.org/security-advisory-btcpay-server-2-4-2/) said that bug exposed Lightning node credentials and did not touch on-chain hot wallets. Dorier said the team has "traces that pre 2.4.2 vulnerabilities were used" and promised a fuller blog post. Version 2.4.7, released Oct. 29, fixed 85 more findings, one rated critical, per its [GitHub release page](https://github.com/btcpayserver/btcpayserver/releases/tag/v2.4.7).

Dorier [told](https://x.com/NicolasDorier/status/2117107091328639417) operators who had updated since 2.4.2 there is "no reason to panic," and added: "Don't keep too much in your Hot Wallet." BTCPay asked anyone affected to send logs to security@btcpayserver.org.

*In our opinion:* Self-hosting puts the keys and the chores in the merchant's hands, and skipped updates are the bill coming due. The open question is the exact way in, which the promised write-up should answer. Watch for a loss estimate and whether the attacker's posted addresses move.

articles.title: Anza Tells Solana Validators to Guard Against 9.8-Rated Linux Bug
articles.excerpt: Ubuntu still lists no fixed kernel for CVE-2026-98432. Solana Foundation staff gave validators three stopgap settings to use until a patch ships.
articles.body_md:
Anza, a lead Solana software developer, told mainnet validators on Sunday to act now on a Linux kernel flaw rated 9.8 out of 10. Ubuntu, the system Anza builds for, has no fixed kernel out yet.

The warning was labeled "Action Required," [The Defiant reported](https://cryptonews.net/news/security/33686402/). No attack on a Solana validator has been reported.

**The bug under the node**

The flaw, CVE-2026-98432, sits in how Linux sets up IPv4 TCP connections, per the kernel's own [advisory](https://lists.openwall.net/linux-cve-announce/2026/10/15/1). Two processor cores can race, and one can free a piece of memory the other is still reading. Researchers at Anthropic built an exploit that ran commands as root on a server with a Multipath TCP listener, [BleepingComputer reported](https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/critical-linux-kernel-flaw-allows-remote-root-attacks-on-mptcp-servers/). Red Hat rated it lower, at 5.9, because the race is hard to win.

Root means full control of the machine. A validator keeps its identity key on that machine, so a takeover could expose it, and a kernel failure could knock it offline. Anza's guidance says the separate withdraw authority, which controls staked funds, should never sit on the server.

**Three stopgaps**

Tim Garcia, validator relations lead at the Solana Foundation, gave Ubuntu operators three steps, [TokenPost reported](https://www.tokenpost.com/news/technology/46064): block incoming TCP packets carrying IPv4 options, turn off Multipath TCP and turn off TCP request socket migration. They are not a fix. The upstream kernel fix exists, but Ubuntu's [tracker](https://ubuntu.com/security/CVE-2026-98432) listed versions 22.04 through 26.10 as vulnerable with work in progress. BleepingComputer said there were no confirmed reports of exploitation in the wild.

*In our opinion:* Kernel upkeep is dull work, and dull work is where validators get caught. Solana's speed rests on a few thousand Linux boxes, and their weakest kernel matters as much as any code on chain. Watch for Ubuntu's patched kernel and how fast operators reboot into it.

articles.title: China's Communist Party Orders Graft Probes Into Crypto, Blockchain
articles.excerpt: The resolution adds no trading ban. It tells party investigators to chase bribes hidden in virtual currency and blockchain, and to lean on big data.
articles.body_md:
China's Communist Party has told its anti-corruption investigators to go after bribes moved through crypto. A resolution adopted Oct. 29 and published in full by state news agency [Xinhua](https://english.news.cn/20261101/16d34cfc97f04b8d925baf68d2963706/c.html) on Sunday names virtual currency and blockchain as channels of graft.

The order is aimed at officials. It is a party discipline document, so it adds no new ban and doesn't change the status of any token, [Yahoo](https://www.yahoo.com/news/world/articles/china-puts-crypto-anti-corruption-143009392.html) and [BlockchainReporter](https://blockchainreporter.net/china-crypto-blockchain-corruption-crackdown/) both noted. Crypto trading is already banned on the mainland.

**One sentence, four channels**

In Xinhua's official English translation, the party says it will "resolutely combat corruption committed via the internet, virtual currency, cross-border capital, and blockchain." The same passage targets hidden graft, such as assets held under someone else's name and "white gloves," the middlemen who hold money for officials.

It also calls for a "big data platform for overseeing the exercise of power in the public sector," the [South China Morning Post](https://www.scmp.com/news/china/politics/article/3372899/communist-party-pledges-reach-deeper-chinas-tech-digital-platform-sectors) and BlockchainReporter reported. The Chinese text runs about 17,000 characters, [Xinhua said](https://www2.xinhuanet.com/politics/leaders/20261101/1a565900cd184863a3230e3bdc4a46eb/c.html).

**How a crypto bribe gets traced**

A blockchain is a public ledger. Every transfer between wallet addresses stays on record, so a payment can be followed years later even when wallets carry no names. The weak spot for anyone hiding money is the moment coins are swapped for cash and land in a bank account.

That is how investigators caught Yao Qian, the former head of the People's Bank of China's digital currency institute, according to a state TV documentary that aired Jan. 14. It said he took 2,000 ether in 2018 from a crypto businessman whose token sale he helped, and that investigators traced the coins to his wallet and to a 2021 sale of 370 ether for about 10 million yuan, [China News Service](http://www.chinanews.com.cn/gn/2026/01-14/10551970.shtml) and the [SCMP](https://www.scmp.com/news/china/politics/article/3340038/how-chinese-corruption-busters-are-tracking-down-bribes-paid-cryptocurrency) reported. The documentary said Yao accepted the findings. He was expelled from the party in November 2024 and handed to prosecutors. Black Mint found no public statement from Yao or a lawyer for him.

*In our opinion: the crypto clause is one sentence, but it sits in a resolution adopted by the full Central Committee, and the Yao case shows the playbook: follow the coins until they touch a bank. The risk falls on officials and their fixers who parked wealth in tokens. The thing to watch is whether discipline commissions start citing crypto in published case notices.*

articles.title: Customers Pull a Net $3.64B From Binance as Withdrawals Return
articles.excerpt: Withdrawals beat deposits by $3.64 billion in Binance's first nine and a half hours back. The exchange says that is 2.1% of assets and the pace is easing.
articles.body_md:
Binance customers took out about $3.64 billion more than they put in during the first nine and a half hours after withdrawals reopened Sunday, the exchange said. It is the first hard number on how much the $6.3 billion hack has shaken trust.

Between 1 a.m. and 10:30 a.m. ET, Binance processed $4.65 billion in withdrawals and $1.01 billion in deposits, it [said on X](https://x.com/binance/status/2116926305254133892). It put the net outflow at 2.1% of its $171 billion in assets under management. Withdrawal volumes "have declined and are stabilising as expected" after an early spike, while deposits "have remained substantial," Binance said. [Reuters](https://www.devdiscourse.com/article/international/4000334-binance-sees-net-outflows-of-364-billion-after-resumption-of-withdrawals) and [Il Sole 24 Ore](https://www.ilsole24ore.com/art/binance-ripresa-attivita-registra-deflussi-364-miliardi-AJ53ED1B) carried the same figures.

An outside count lines up. DefiLlama's dashboard showed more than $3.5 billion in net outflows from Binance on Sunday, [Reuters reported](https://www.devdiscourse.com/article/international/4000329-binance-sees-spike-in-customers-pulling-funds-out-after-covering-bulk-of-stolen-63-billion). Binance did not comment on that data.

**Why the net number is the one to read**

While withdrawals are frozen, nobody can test whether an exchange still holds their coins. Reopening lets each customer run that test by moving coins to a wallet they control. Gross withdrawals measure how busy the exit door was. The net figure subtracts fresh deposits, so it tracks the money that actually left the building.

**Solana is back, other coins wait**

Solana withdrawals for SOL, USDT and USDC [returned](https://x.com/binance/status/2116851716448718901) at about 6:15 a.m. ET. Black Mint [reported earlier Sunday](https://blackmint.markets/news/binance-reopens-withdrawals-nine-networks/) that Solana was still closed. By 7:36 a.m. ET all 15 networks and assets in the first phase were running, Binance said, after TON, Sui and Zcash [joined the list](https://x.com/binance/status/2116871932075516174). The exchange said it is still testing the rest.

Binance also said it has now covered 95% of the stolen assets, up from the 90% it gave Saturday, Reuters reported. The remainder is in less liquid tokens that may take longer to buy, the exchange said.

Bitcoin traded at $78,071 around noon ET, up 0.7% over 24 hours, per CoinGecko.

*In our opinion: losing 2.1% of assets in a morning is a bruise rather than a run, as long as the pace keeps slowing the way Binance says it is. The fuller verdict comes when the remaining networks reopen and the last 5% of stolen tokens is bought back. Watch the next proof-of-reserves snapshot and whether Monday's net outflow comes in smaller than Sunday's.*

articles.title: OPEC+ Holds December Output Steady With Brent Near $118
articles.excerpt: Seven OPEC+ producers changed nothing for December and set up a Nov. 29 showdown over 2027 quotas, with Brent near its highest since April.
articles.body_md:
Seven OPEC+ producers kept their December oil output targets unchanged on Sunday, pushing the hard choices to a Nov. 29 meeting while Brent crude sits near its highest level since April.

Saudi Arabia, Russia, Iraq, Kuwait, Kazakhstan, Algeria and Oman met online and agreed to keep September's required production levels for December, OPEC said in a [statement](https://www.opec.org/pr-detail/2033620-1-november-2026.html). The group will keep meeting monthly, and the next session is Nov. 29, the statement said. [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/31/opec-oil-output-targets-december.html) reported the same decision.

The price backdrop is steep. December Brent futures settled up $2.76, or 2.4%, at $117.64 a barrel on Friday before expiring, CNBC reported, and U.S. crude ended at $104.12. Traders were bracing for a possible escalation in the U.S.-Iran war after Tuesday's U.S. midterm elections, according to the report.

**How the quota math works**

Each month OPEC+ sets a required production level for each member, a ceiling meant to keep supply in line with demand. These seven spent much of 2026 raising those ceilings and finished unwinding a 1.65 million-barrel-a-day cut in September, CNBC reported. Another layer of about 2 million barrels a day of cuts runs through the end of 2026. For now the ceiling is not what holds supply back. Gulf members are still pumping well below their targets because the war has disrupted exports, per CNBC.

"Today's decision was the easy one," Jorge Leon, an analyst at Rystad, said in remarks carried by CNBC. The Nov. 29 meeting is expected to set 2027 quotas, and the International Energy Agency has warned of excess supply next year if Gulf flows return to normal, the report said.

**The road from oil to bitcoin**

Oil feeds into fuel, freight and airfares, so a price near $118 can keep inflation high. High inflation makes it harder for the Federal Reserve to cut rates, and rate expectations move crypto prices along with stocks. Bitcoin traded at $78,071 around noon ET, up 0.7% over 24 hours, per CoinGecko.

*In our opinion: a meeting that changes nothing still sends a message, and this one says the group would rather wait out the war than guess at it. The real fight is Nov. 29, when 2027 quotas meet an IEA surplus warning. If Brent holds above $110 into that date, the Fed's inflation problem gets harder, and crypto traders will feel it in their rate bets.*

articles.title: Binance Reopens Withdrawals on Nine Networks After $6.3B Hack
articles.excerpt: Bitcoin went first, then ether, BNB and stablecoins. Binance says all withdrawals now come from new wallet addresses; Solana isn't back yet.
articles.body_md:
Binance reopened withdrawals on at least nine blockchain networks by 5:48 a.m. ET Sunday, three days after a theft of about $6.3 billion from its hot wallets was announced.

Bitcoin went first. Early Sunday the exchange [said on X](https://x.com/binance/status/2116777408074600621) that the bitcoin network was the "first batch" of phase one. Ethereum and BNB Smart Chain followed for ETH, BNB, USDT and USDC, and later posts added XRP, Base, Dogecoin, Optimism, Arbitrum and Tron, according to Binance's [latest update](https://x.com/binance/status/2116844881448743094). [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/31/binance-hack-asset-coverage-withdrawals.html) also reported the restart.

Withdrawals are the part customers can test for themselves. Binance said Saturday that it had replaced 90% of the stolen assets and that holdings of 10 coins, including BTC, ETH, USDT, BNB, SOL and XRP, are fully backed. Black Mint [reported that pledge](https://blackmint.markets/news/binance-replaces-90-percent-stolen-crypto-withdrawals-sunday/) on Oct. 31.

**Withdrawals now come from new addresses**

A hot wallet is an exchange wallet kept online so it can sign customer withdrawals quickly. That speed is also what makes it a target. Binance [said Sunday](https://x.com/binance/status/2116785774540787920) it has added newly generated addresses to its proof-of-reserves list, the public set of wallets anyone can check on-chain, and that all withdrawals will now be processed from them.

The refill is paid for out of three pots: SAFU, the exchange's emergency fund for users, part of its futures insurance fund and corporate treasury money, Binance said in a statement carried by CNBC. The missing 10% sits in tokens outside its top 10. Binance said those are less liquid and may take longer to buy.

**What Binance hasn't said**

The exchange still hasn't explained how the attacker got in. It first pointed to a compromised engineer's laptop; co-CEO Richard Teng later said the attack was more complex than one person's access, CNBC reported. Binance declined to give CNBC further details. The FBI said Saturday that North Korea was responsible.

The Solana network was not on Binance's list of reopened networks as of 5:48 a.m. ET. Its posts gave no date for the rest, saying only that more networks will return in phases as security checks finish.

*In our opinion: a working withdrawal button is a promise customers can check in their own wallets. The next tests are the networks still closed, including Solana, and the last 10% held in smaller tokens. Watch Binance's next recovery update for both, and for an account of how the attacker got in.*

articles.title: FBI Says North Korea Stole $6B From Binance, Names 628 Addresses
articles.excerpt: The FBI named TraderTraitor and asked exchanges and DeFi services to block 628 addresses it says hold or held the stolen funds, mostly on Ethereum.
articles.body_md:
The FBI said Saturday that North Korea was responsible for the theft of more than $6 billion in crypto from Binance on or about Oct. 29. The bureau had earlier said only that it was [aware of the incident](https://www.nextgov.com/cybersecurity/2026/10/fbi-involved-response-63-billion-binance-hack-linked-north-korea/416946/).

Until now, the North Korea link came from private firms. Black Mint [reported Oct. 30](https://blackmint.markets/news/binance-hack-north-korea-tradertraitor/) that TRM Labs tied the attack to TraderTraitor, a North Korean state hacking unit, and Chainalysis said the same in its [own analysis](https://www.chainalysis.com/blog/binance-exploit-latest-findings-and-response/). The [FBI alert](https://www.fbi.gov/investigate/cyber/alerts/2026/north-korea-responsible-for-6-billion-binance-attack) now uses that name too, the same one it gave the group behind the [$1.5 billion Bybit theft](https://www.ic3.gov/PSA/2025/PSA250226) in February 2025.

**628 addresses on a block list**

The FBI, working with the Secret Service and IRS Criminal Investigation, said the hackers have been converting stolen assets mainly into ether. The bureau expects them to move next through DeFi apps and instant swap services.

How that laundering works: an instant swap service trades one coin for another in minutes, often without an account, so each hop makes the trail harder to follow. A block list fights back. Once an address is public, exchanges and node operators can refuse any transaction that touches it.

The alert lists 608 Ethereum addresses, 19 bitcoin addresses and one Solana address that it says hold or held stolen funds. It asks exchanges, DeFi services, blockchain analytics firms and THORChain node operators to block transfers linked to them. [Reuters](https://www.devdiscourse.com/article/international/4000213-fbi-links-north-korea-to-theft-of-6-billion-frombinance) also reported the FBI finding Saturday.

**What it changes for Binance users**

Customer balances are a separate track. Binance has said it will cover customer losses, and on Saturday it said 90% of the stolen crypto had been replaced, with withdrawals set to start reopening in phases Sunday, Nov. 1, [Reuters reported](https://www.channelnewsasia.com/business/binance-replenishes-90-assets-stolen-in-security-incident-6509761).

North Korea has denied it is behind such hacks in the past, the [BBC reported](https://www.bbc.com/news/live/cqrmynd3042gt).

*In our opinion: the hunt now moves from the exchange to everyone downstream of it. Every swap desk and node operator that honors this list makes the stolen ether harder to cash out, and every one that ignores it becomes the weak link. Watch whether the FBI adds addresses as the funds move, and whether Binance's withdrawal restart on Sunday runs smoothly.*

articles.title: Binance Says 90% of Stolen Crypto Is Replaced as Withdrawals Near
articles.excerpt: Ten coins, including bitcoin and ether, are fully backed again, the exchange says. Withdrawals are set to restart Sunday, with a proof users can check due Nov. 3.
articles.body_md:
Binance said Saturday it has replaced 90% of the crypto stolen in Thursday's $6.3 billion hack, up from about 80% a day earlier, a [Reuters report](https://www.channelnewsasia.com/business/binance-replenishes-90-assets-stolen-in-security-incident-6509761) carried by CNA shows. Customer holdings of 10 coins, including bitcoin, ether, USDT, BNB, SOL and XRP, are now fully backed, the exchange said.

That leaves one day before the real test. Binance said it remains on track to start reopening withdrawals in phases on Sunday, Nov. 1, once security checks are done.

**Where the money came from**

The last 10% is in smaller, thinly traded tokens that take longer to buy in size, Binance said, so it keeps buying them on exchanges and through over-the-counter desks. To pay for the refill, it is drawing on part of SAFU, the emergency fund for users it set up in 2018, part of its futures insurance fund and company money, [ChainCatcher reported](https://www.chaincatcher.com/en/article/2300674) from the update. Binance has pledged to top SAFU back up to about $1 billion. It had already set aside about $6.34 billion. Separately, about $3 billion of the stolen assets is frozen on-chain, Binance said in its [Oct. 30 notice](https://www.binance.com/en/support/announcement/detail/c5a8729a97ac486d963784d96c5642d7).

**How the proof works**

A proof of reserves compares what an exchange holds with what it owes customers at one moment. Binance took that snapshot at 00:00 UTC on Oct. 31. It then builds a cryptographic proof, called a zk-SNARK, that lets each user check that their own balance was counted without seeing anyone else's. Binance said the math takes 40 to 50 hours to run, so users should be able to check by about Nov. 3. The initial figures show reserve ratios at or above 100% for all 10 coins, [The Crypto Times reported](https://www.cryptotimes.io/2026/10/31/binance-reports-90-replenishment-updates-por-after-6-3b-hack/). A snapshot shows one moment, not every risk on the books.

BNB traded near $705 at 11:56 a.m. ET, up 0.8% in 24 hours, per CoinGecko.

*In our opinion: Sunday's reopening is the moment that counts, because a smooth restart shows the refill is real and a stalled one tells users more than any statement can. The Nov. 3 proof is the second check, and it is worth more than the headline 90% because each user can verify it for themselves. The last 10% is the slow part, and how long those small tokens take to buy is the date to watch.*

articles.title: Jobs Report, Treasury Borrowing and the BoE Set Up a Busy Week
articles.excerpt: Treasury sets its borrowing plan Wednesday, the Bank of England decides Thursday and October jobs land Friday, with bitcoin near $77,359.
articles.body_md:
Washington tells markets how much it plans to borrow on Wednesday, and how many jobs the economy added in October on Friday. Bitcoin heads into that stretch near $77,359, according to [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/bitcoin) at 6:02 a.m. ET Saturday.

It is the first full week since the Fed held its target range at 3.75% to 4% on Oct. 28, per the [Fed's statement](https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevents/pressreleases/monetary20261028a.htm). The next Fed meeting is Dec. 8 and 9, per its [meeting calendar](https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm).

## The dates

- **Monday, Nov. 2, 3 p.m. ET:** Treasury releases its borrowing estimates, per its [refunding page](https://home.treasury.gov/policy-issues/financing-the-government/quarterly-refunding/most-recent-quarterly-refunding-documents).
- **Tuesday, Nov. 3, 10 a.m. ET:** September job openings (JOLTS), per the [BLS calendar](https://www.bls.gov/schedule/2026/11_sched.htm).
- **Wednesday, Nov. 4, 8:30 a.m. ET:** Treasury's quarterly refunding statement.
- **Thursday, Nov. 5, 7 a.m. ET:** The Bank of England's decision, at noon London time, per its [MPC dates](https://www.bankofengland.co.uk/monetary-policy/upcoming-mpc-dates). Bank Rate sits at 3.75%. Third-quarter productivity and costs follow at 8:30 a.m. ET.
- **Friday, Nov. 6, 8:30 a.m. ET:** The October jobs report, per the [BLS schedule](https://www.bls.gov/schedule/news_release/empsit.htm).

## How the refunding works

Every quarter, Treasury says how much it will sell in notes and bonds and how much of that is new cash. In August it offered $125 billion to refund about $96.3 billion of maturing debt, raising about $28.7 billion in new money, per its [August statement](https://home.treasury.gov/news/press-releases/sb0590). Bigger sales mean more bonds for investors to absorb, which can pull cash away from other assets.

Spot bitcoin ETFs saw about $643.2 million in net outflows on Friday, Oct. 30, according to [Farside Investors](https://farside.co.uk/btc/).

*In our opinion:* The jobs report gets the headlines, but Wednesday's borrowing plan sets the price of money, and nobody throws it a parade. Watch how much new cash Treasury asks for and whether Friday's payrolls move the odds for the Fed's Dec. 9 decision.

articles.title: Bitcoin ETFs Lose $643 Million Friday, Wiping Out the Week's Gains
articles.excerpt: Spot ether ETFs shed $155.7 million too, their fifth straight day of withdrawals. BlackRock's IBIT and Fidelity's FBTC led the bitcoin exits.
articles.body_md:
Investors pulled $643.2 million out of U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs on Friday, Farside Investors data shows. That one day erased the week's gains and left the funds $202.4 million in the red for Oct. 26-30.

Spot ether ETFs lost another $155.7 million, their fifth straight day of withdrawals. Ether funds shed $431.4 million over the week.

**Four funds did most of the selling**

- BlackRock's IBIT: $233.7 million out
- Fidelity's FBTC: $201.0 million out
- ARK's ARKB: $129.5 million out
- Grayscale's GBTC: $53.3 million out

Bitwise's BITB lost $25.7 million. No bitcoin fund took in new money on the day.

How the flows work: an ETF share is backed by coins the fund holds. When big brokers called authorized participants hand shares back for redemption, the fund gives up bitcoin or cash and its holdings shrink. A net outflow means more shares were redeemed than created that day. The money also carries a cost. IBIT charges 0.25% a year, while GBTC still charges 1.50%, Farside's fee table shows.

**A big week, then a reversal**

The bitcoin funds had taken in $440.8 million from Monday through Thursday. Even after Friday, they hold a net $57.0 billion in lifetime inflows since their January 2024 launch, by Farside's count.

Friday's outflows came as investigators chased more than $6 billion stolen from Binance this week, [CNBC reported](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/30/binance-hack-stolen-crypto-recovery.html). Farside's figures show where money moved, not why, and no fund issuer has given a reason for the withdrawals.

Bitcoin was near $77,100 at 11:56 p.m. ET Friday, down 1.1% in 24 hours and 4.3% over seven days, per CoinGecko. Ether was near $2,238, up 0.2% on the day.

*In our opinion: the number that stands out is the ether side, five down days in a row and $431.4 million gone, while bitcoin funds were still adding money until Friday. Monday's flow print is the first test of whether Friday was a one-day reaction or the start of a run. Lifetime inflows of $57.0 billion give the funds a lot of room before that total looks different.*

Source: Farside Investors. Prices powered by CoinGecko.

articles.title: CFTC Chair Cites $6.3B Binance Hack in Push for Exchange Registration
articles.excerpt: Michael Selig says the theft proves the CFTC's case for a federal option for offshore exchanges. Registration stays optional; comments close Dec. 14.
articles.body_md:
CFTC Chairman Michael Selig said Friday that the roughly $6.3 billion Binance theft "proves our exact point" for the agency's plan to let crypto exchanges register with it. Public comments on that plan are due Dec. 14.

Selig spoke in a CNBC interview the day after the hack, [Yahoo Finance reported](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/crypto/articles/binance-hacked-cftc-chair-says-173241959.html). "The real issue here is that these are unregulated offshore exchanges, and they don't have the same sorts of safeguards that we have in our financial markets here in the U.S.," he said.

**An option for exchanges**

The plan is an [advance notice of proposed rulemaking](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/10/13/2026-20888/regulation-crypto-asset-transactions-and-regulation-crypto-asset-markets) the CFTC published Oct. 13. It covers two sets of rules, Regulation Crypto Asset Transactions (CTX) and Regulation Crypto Asset Markets (CAM).

How it works: an advance notice is the earliest step in federal rulemaking. It asks the public for input before the agency writes an actual proposed rule, which then needs its own comment period before anything becomes final. Nothing in this notice binds an exchange today.

In a [Wall Street Journal op-ed posted by the CFTC](https://www.cftc.gov/PressRoom/SpeechesTestimony/seligstatement100526), Selig said the rules wouldn't force crypto trading onto CFTC-registered platforms. The agency lacks that power without Congress, he wrote. Exchanges that opt in could offer retail customers margined, leveraged or financed trading, which state-licensed venues can't, he wrote. On Friday he said registered venues would face "the same sorts of cybersecurity safeguards that we have in our markets today."

**Tracing the money**

Selig also said the public blockchain record gives investigators "a very good shot" at following the stolen funds, even through mixers such as Tornado Cash, and that the CFTC would help law enforcement. He said the attack hit the systems around the blockchain, while the blockchain itself held up.

Binance has said it [reserved more than $6.34 billion](https://x.com/binance/status/2116121748555153621) of company money to cover users' losses.

*In our opinion: the timing gives the CFTC its strongest case yet, but the limit is written in its own op-ed: registration stays optional until Congress acts. The stake is plain enough, with $6.3 billion gone from a platform outside U.S. market rules. The next date that counts is Dec. 14, when comments close, and the bigger test is whether any large offshore venue says it will opt in.*

articles.title: Binance Sets Aside $6.34B for Hack Losses, Buys Missing Tokens
articles.excerpt: Binance says $5 billion of the reserve already sits in the stolen tokens and it is buying the rest, though some of those coins trade thinly.
articles.body_md:
Binance said at 6:55 a.m. ET Friday that it has reserved more than $6.34 billion of company money to cover Thursday's theft and has begun recovering affected assets for users.

That covers its estimate of about $6.3 billion taken, the largest crypto theft on record by [TRM Labs' count](https://www.trmlabs.com/resources/blog/north-korea-steals-usd-6-36-billion-from-binance-in-the-largest-hack-in-history). In a [post on X](https://x.com/binance/status/2116121748555153621), Binance said $5 billion of the reserve is already held in "the exact token assets that were impacted." It is buying the rest on exchanges and through over-the-counter (OTC) desks, which arrange large private trades. Binance said that step "can take longer because some tokens may have low liquidity and OTC settlement also takes time."

**Why the tokens have to match**

How it works: a customer who kept 1,000 units of a small token on Binance is owed 1,000 units of that token, not its dollar value. Co-founder Yi He [said on X](https://x.com/heyibinance/status/2116124832584904742) that the SAFU fund, Binance's emergency reserve for users, and the firm's own holdings are mostly in assets such as bitcoin and ether, and that it is buying "all the stolen altcoins in fully matching amounts." Buying thinly traded coins in size can push their prices up, which slows the work.

The $6.34 billion does not count about $3 billion that partners have frozen on-chain, Binance said. Those coins can't move, but still have to be recovered.

The cause is also less settled than it looked overnight. Binance [said at 4:47 a.m. ET](https://x.com/binance/status/2116089661408108712) that its first finding pointed to a compromised laptop, but its team "has uncovered additional points of breach."

Withdrawals stay paused. Binance [said at 12:36 a.m. ET](https://x.com/binance/status/2116026356740034858) that it expects to restart them within 48 hours, after "a security revamp of the withdrawal service." That window runs to about 12:36 a.m. ET Sunday. Deposits are working normally, Binance said.

BNB, the token tied to Binance's BNB Chain, traded at $698 at 12:03 p.m. ET, down 6.8% over 24 hours, according to [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/bnb).

*In our opinion:* Binance has now put a dollar figure on its promise, and it covers the whole loss before any frozen money comes back. The cost lands on Binance's own balance sheet, while holders of small tokens it must buy back could see sharp price swings in the meantime. The tests to watch are the withdrawal restart before Sunday and the updated Proof of Reserves, Binance's public tally of what it holds against what it owes customers.

articles.title: Intel Sinks 29% on Weak Forecast as Nasdaq Slides Over 2%
articles.excerpt: Intel guided fourth-quarter revenue to $15 billion to $16 billion, short of the $17.07 billion analysts expected, and sees the PC slump lasting into 2027.
articles.body_md:
Intel shares fell about 29% Friday morning after the chipmaker forecast weak holiday-quarter sales, helping pull the Nasdaq Composite down 2.3% by 11:06 a.m. ET, [AP reported](https://apnews.com/article/stock-markets-ai-alphabet-oil-16c266731fdf64178f38070af2b42497).

The drop put Intel on track to lose more than $137 billion in market value, [Reuters reported](https://www.rte.ie/news/business/2026/1030/1597308-intel-quarterly-results/). [CNBC said](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/30/amazon-intel-earnings-big-tech-ai-spending-concerns.html) the stock was headed for its worst day since 1974.

In its [results release](https://www.intc.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/1786/intel-reports-third-quarter-2026-financial-results), Intel forecast fourth-quarter revenue of $15 billion to $16 billion and adjusted earnings of 25 cents a share. Analysts expected $17.07 billion and 43 cents, according to LSEG data cited by [Reuters](https://www.streetinsider.com/Reuters/Intel+signals+slower+growth+as+PC+market+remains+under+pressure/27257618.html). The quarter just ended went better: revenue rose 21% to $16.5 billion, and adjusted earnings of 52 cents beat the 40-cent estimate.

**Why the forecast mattered more**

How it works: a share price is a bet on future profits, so a company's forecast, called guidance, often moves the stock more than the quarter it just reported. Intel's trouble starts with memory. Suppliers have shifted capacity toward the high-bandwidth memory used in AI servers, which raises the cost of building a PC and weighs on demand, Reuters reported.

"We see the PC slowdown continuing at least through the first half of next year," finance chief David Zinsner said in the release. Intel also expects an explosion this month at its plant in Israel, which killed two workers, to cost about $600 million in revenue over two quarters, [CNBC reported](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/29/intel-intc-q3-earnings-report-2026-.html). Zinsner said Intel does not expect positive cash flow this year.

There is a stronger side to the report. Data center and AI revenue jumped 78% to $7.3 billion, CNBC said, and the stock was up about 150% this year before the results. CEO Lip-Bu Tan said Intel expects to announce "a couple of customers" for its contract chipmaking business over the next two quarters.

The selling spread. AMD fell 9.3% and a broad chip index lost 5.7% in early trading, [Reuters reported](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/nasdaq-futures-sink-amazon-intel-114737736.html). Crypto was lower too: bitcoin traded at $77,512 at 12:03 p.m. ET, down 5% over 24 hours, according to [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/bitcoin).

*In our opinion:* Wall Street is showing little patience for heavy AI-era spending that doesn't turn into cash soon. More than $137 billion of Intel's value was at stake Friday morning, and the rest of the chip group paid part of that bill. The next real test is whether Tan names those outside foundry customers, because that is where the turnaround case lives.

articles.title: TRM Labs Ties $6.36B Binance Hack to North Korea's TraderTraitor
articles.excerpt: The attacker pre-signed 50 Ethereum authorizations and still holds about $2.4 billion in bitcoin and ether that no issuer can freeze, TRM Labs said.
articles.body_md:
Blockchain analytics firm TRM Labs said it believes with "high confidence" that TraderTraitor, a North Korean state-backed hacking unit, carried out Thursday's theft of about $6.36 billion from Binance.

That puts a name on the largest crypto theft on record. In a [blog post](https://www.trmlabs.com/resources/blog/north-korea-steals-usd-6-36-billion-from-binance-in-the-largest-hack-in-history), TRM said the money left Binance wallets on 10 blockchains, most of it in about 20 minutes starting at 4:05 p.m. ET. The FBI [named the same group](https://www.ic3.gov/PSA/2025/PSA250226) for the $1.5 billion Bybit theft in February 2025.

Chainalysis CEO Jonathan Levin also said the attack was likely TraderTraitor's work, [CNBC reported](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/30/billions-in-crypto-frozen-in-binance-hack-heres-what-happens-next-.html). Neither is a government finding.

**Signatures prepared in advance**

TRM said preparation began at least 36 hours earlier, funded through Tornado Cash, a service that hides where crypto came from.

How the Ethereum leg worked: EIP-7702, added in Ethereum's May 2025 upgrade, lets an ordinary wallet hand its behavior to a smart contract by signing an authorization. Each wallet keeps a running transaction count, and an authorization only works at the right count. TRM said the attacker had 50 signed authorizations ready for 50 counts in a row, so one would fit no matter how many withdrawals Binance processed. One matched, and a sweeper contract emptied the wallet.

Wallets on nine other chains paid the attacker through ordinary signed transfers. In TRM's view, that points to a compromise of Binance's hot-wallet signing system, which approves payouts. Binance said late Thursday that an engineer's [compromised laptop](https://www.binance.com/en/support/announcement/detail/c5a8729a97ac486d963784d96c5642d7) may be the cause, and it has not published a full root cause.

**What's frozen and what isn't**

TRM counted about $2.7 billion frozen by Tether, Circle, Ripple, World Liberty Financial and Arbitrum's Security Council. The attacker still holds more than 420,000 ETH and 18,270 BTC, about $2.4 billion that no issuer can freeze, the firm said.

Bitcoin was at $77,578 at 6 a.m. ET, down 3.2% in 24 hours, and BNB at $702, down 6.2%, per [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/bnb). Black Mint found no public response from North Korea.

*In our opinion:* If the attribution holds, this is TraderTraitor's second record theft in under two years, about four times Bybit's size. The $2.4 billion in bitcoin and ether is the part that matters now, because only tracing and cooperating exchanges can stop it. Watch for the coins to hit bridges and over-the-counter desks, and for Binance's post-mortem to say whether one laptop really reached the signing system.

articles.title: Binance Says Laptop Breach May Be Behind $6.3B Hack, Vows Full Cover
articles.excerpt: Binance puts the hack at about $6.3 billion, names a compromised engineer's laptop as a possible cause and says it will cover all losses as withdrawals stay shut.
articles.body_md:
Binance said at 10:25 PM ET Thursday that a compromised engineer's laptop may be behind a security incident it now puts at about $6.3 billion.

That is the first named cause and the first total from the exchange itself. In an [X post](https://x.com/binance/status/2115993361517891592) linking its [announcement](https://www.binance.com/en/support/announcement/detail/c5a8729a97ac486d963784d96c5642d7), Binance said the laptop "allowed an attacker to gain access to a service container and submit unauthorized withdrawal transactions." It said it found "no evidence of any wallet private key leak" and has revoked the affected address authorisation.

At that size it would be the largest crypto theft on record, the [South China Morning Post](https://www.scmp.com/business/cryptocurrency/article/3372664/binance-pledges-cover-losses-after-us6-billion-crypto-hack) noted, ahead of the $1.5 billion taken from Bybit in February 2025, which the [FBI tied to North Korea](https://www.ic3.gov/PSA/2025/PSA250226).

How it works: exchanges keep most coins in offline cold storage and a smaller pool in hot wallets that pay out withdrawals automatically. A service container is a walled-off piece of software on a server that does one job, such as sending payout requests. If Binance's early account holds, the attacker never needed the vault keys. Access to the system that asks for withdrawals was enough to move coins out.

Now the money. Binance said about $3 billion has been frozen on-chain with partners, which leaves roughly $3.3 billion not yet frozen by its own numbers. It said it "will cover all losses from the SAFU fund and the company's funds," that user funds are safe, and that it will publish an updated proof of reserves after the fix.

All deposits and withdrawals are suspended, wider than the partial pause earlier in the evening. Co-founder Yi He [said at 10:32 PM](https://x.com/heyibinance/status/2115995324825370777) withdrawals will reopen once a security scan finishes, with no time given. She also [said](https://x.com/heyibinance/status/2115962957880602653) the Arbitrum Security Council froze about $30.5 million, and Coinbase CEO Brian Armstrong [said](https://x.com/brian_armstrong/status/2115976950376210483) Coinbase is blocking sends to compromised wallets.

BNB traded at $717.66 at 11:58 PM ET, down 3.8% over 24 hours, and bitcoin at $78,008, down 2.2%, per [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/bnb).

*In our opinion:* A named cause and a written promise to pay are the two things customers needed tonight, and Binance has now put both on the record. The open question is the $3.3 billion that isn't frozen, which SAFU and company funds would have to fill. Watch for a restart time on withdrawals and the post-mortem, which should show whether one laptop really opened the door.

articles.title: Bank of Japan Says 2% Goal Is Met for First Time Since 2013
articles.excerpt: The Bank of Japan held at 1.25% but called underlying inflation consistent with 2% for the first time since 2013, clearing its own bar for more hikes.
articles.body_md:
The Bank of Japan said Friday in Tokyo, late Thursday ET, that underlying inflation is "generally consistent" with its 2% target, a first since it set that goal in 2013.

Until now, the bank had only said inflation was approaching 2%, [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/30/boj-inflation-target-rates.html) reported. The bank held its overnight rate at about 1.25%, the highest since 1995, in an 8-1 vote, according to its [policy statement](https://www.boj.or.jp/en/mopo/mpmdeci/mpr_2026/k261030a.pdf). CNBC said board member Hajime Takata dissented in favor of a hike to 1.5%.

The [outlook report](https://www.boj.or.jp/en/mopo/mpmdeci/mpr_2026/k261030b.pdf) raised the fiscal 2027 forecast for consumer prices excluding fresh food to 2.6% from 2.4%, and said price risks are "skewed to the upside" as firms lean more toward raising wages and prices. The other side: experts told CNBC that energy subsidies are holding headline price numbers down, so part of the pressure is masked.

The bank also sped up its exit from the stock market. Starting January 2027, it will sell its exchange-traded funds at about 860 billion yen a year at book value, up from 330 billion, per its [ETF decision](https://www.boj.or.jp/en/mopo/mpmdeci/mpr_2026/k261030c.pdf). That cuts the time to finish selling from about 112 years to about 43. Brisk, by central bank standards.

How it works: "underlying" inflation strips out jumpy items like fresh food and energy, so it shows whether price rises are spreading through wages and services. Saying it has reached 2% is the test the bank set for itself before raising rates further. Why crypto readers care: for years, near-zero Japanese rates made the yen a cheap currency to borrow and invest elsewhere. Higher Japanese rates make that trade costlier, and unwinding it can pull money out of risk assets, crypto included.

All 16 economists in a CNBC survey expect the bank to set up a hike in December or January.

*In our opinion:* Thirteen years of "approaching" just became "consistent," and that one word change is the bank clearing its own bar for more hikes. The stake for crypto is the cheap-yen funding that has backed risk trades worldwide for years. Watch the December meeting and the yen, because a fast move in either can spill into crypto.

articles.title: Binance Pauses Some Withdrawals as $2.54B Frozen After Alleged Multi-Billion Hack
articles.excerpt: Trackers allege $5.7B to $5.8B was taken, which Binance hasn't confirmed. Tether and Circle froze more than 2.3 billion in stablecoins.
articles.body_md:
Binance has paused withdrawals on multiple networks while it investigates what security firms and trackers allege is a multi-billion-dollar hack of its hot wallets. At 7:22 p.m. ET Thursday, the exchange [said](https://x.com/binance/status/2115947325617299903) the "current verified total frozen is $2.54 billion" and that its teams are working closely with law enforcement.

Binance has not called the event a hack, given a loss figure or said who is behind it. At 6:15 p.m. it [said](https://x.com/binance/status/2115930656589119995) withdrawals "will resume as soon as the security issue is fully resolved" and that "user funds remain safe." A spokesperson called the pause a "precautionary measure," [TechCrunch reported](https://techcrunch.com/2026/10/29/binance-pauses-withdrawals-as-hackers-suspected-of-stealing-billions-in-crypto/).

**What the trackers allege**

The outflows began about 4:24 p.m. ET, [Unchained reported](https://unchainedcrypto.com/binance-says-user-funds-are-completely-safe-after-3-5-billion-drains-from-its-hot-wallets/). PeckShieldAlert [posted](https://x.com/PeckShieldAlert/status/2115917332786851967) "Confirmed hack" at 5:22 p.m. At 7:27 p.m., tracker Lookonchain [alleged](https://x.com/lookonchain/status/2115948651554157043) that more than $5.8 billion was stolen and is being sold for other tokens. Arkham data put the total near $5.7 billion, per a post [Arkham shared](https://x.com/arkham/status/2115952424171061288). Binance has not confirmed either number.

**How a stablecoin freeze works**

USDT and USDC are tokens whose issuers can block a wallet address. Once an address is frozen, the tokens in it can't be sent or swapped, but they aren't returned yet. Tether CEO Paolo Ardoino [said](https://x.com/paoloardoino/status/2115918000373346709) the company froze more than 1.567 billion USDT. Circle CEO Jeremy Allaire [said](https://x.com/jerallaire/status/2115916207463481846) Circle froze more than 800 million USDC "in coordination with law enforcement." Coins like ether have no issuer, so they can't be frozen this way.

**Who says they will pay**

Founder Changpeng Zhao, who no longer runs Binance, [wrote](https://x.com/cz_binance/status/2115915423174853077) that it "does look like a hack." At 6:23 p.m. he [replied](https://x.com/cz_binance/status/2115932500006756686) to a post estimating the net loss near $1 billion: "Loss might be a bit higher than that, but will cover." For scale, the FBI [tied](https://www.ic3.gov/PSA/2025/PSA250226) a $1.5 billion theft from Bybit in February 2025 to North Korea.

BNB traded near $703 at 7:45 p.m. ET, down 7.3% in 24 hours, and bitcoin near $78,460, down 3.4%, per CoinGecko.

*In our opinion: The $2.54 billion frozen is the only figure Binance itself stands behind, and the tracker totals are more than twice that. If those totals hold, the alleged theft would be nearly four times the size of Bybit's. Until withdrawals resume, users on the paused networks can't move funds off the exchange. Watch for Binance's own loss figure, a named cause and a date for withdrawals to restart.*
